status: Remaining archived row-identity acceptance is explicit; no new implementation or native failure claimed.
fixed_scope_under_verification: Late-sharing lifecycle plus nullable scalar unique keys and deduplicated complete scalar-row domains for repeatable residual predicates. The native queue, not this source design, determines acceptance.
outstanding_cases: Float/Double identity, including signed zero and NaN payloads.
Fixed composite, nested optional, timezone and bare-Null identities.
Lists, dictionaries, Pg and opaque/resource values.
Keyless volatile predicates or correlated subplans whose evaluation count is observable.
Nonrepeatable producer sharing when spilling is unavailable.
Actual zero-column query acceptance remains separate from the direct-IR generator.

candidate_extensions.classification: Potentially solvable inside new RBO with a narrow serialization-domain extension, but not by widening the current whitelist.
mechanism: Produce raw Pickle String identities before the Replicate hub.
Group the secondary domain on those String identities, not on the original floating/composite columns.
Unpickle domain payloads using the exact original type into fresh IUs and rebind the inner join, residual expressions and subplan captures to those IUs.
Reconstruct the primary bag using serialized identity columns. Keep original primary payload definitions untouched.
proof_obligations: Raw Pickle preserves signed-zero and NaN bits; StablePickle canonicalizes them and is not a substitute for exact row identity.
Use a recursive explicit persisted fixed-value type admission, initially excluding lists/dicts/Pg/resources.

Add a local identity-copy-stability condition. Existing CanDuplicateAggregation intentionally ignores floating reduction/order differences, so two cloned producers can have equal-looking but different raw results. Do not weaken the existing global repeatability gate or assume byte stability from it.
For every accepted type verify Unpickle(Pickle(value)) preserves all observations allowed by admitted residual expressions, not merely SQL equality.
Maintain nonempty zero-column domain handling, original bag multiplicities, and absent optional encodings.
candidate_extensions.limits: No artifact or native proof yet. Source tables show a viable building block, not a complete acceptance claim.

candidate_extensions.case: Bare Null, nested Optional, timezone and fixed scalar containers
candidate_extensions.classification: Potentially solvable with encoded domain keys and exact payload reconstruction.
candidate_extensions.reason: Raw packing includes optional presence, timezone IDs, tuple/struct field order and variant tags. Grouping on the original values can still collapse distinctions or use unsupported hash keys; encoded String grouping is the coherent repair.

candidate_extensions.classification: Requires additional contracts; not a safe small whitelist change.
candidate_extensions.reason: Packing lists consumes iterators and may force previously lazy evaluation. Nonstable dictionary packing uses iterator order; stable packing sorts but canonicalizes nested floats. These representations do not establish a universal observation-preserving, clone-stable identity.

candidate_extensions.case: Volatile predicates and called subplans over duplicate left rows
candidate_extensions.classification: Value-domain deduplication fundamentally cannot preserve per-occurrence evaluation count. A different execution mechanism is required.
alternatives: An occurrence ID assigned once before sharing could work, but KqpStreamEnumerate currently guarantees only a counter per stream/flow/list evaluation; it is not globally unique across tasks and copies can reorder rows. It needs planner ownership, distribution and no-copy guarantees.

When block joins are already enabled and supported, a generated equal constant key could route a left-family non-equi join through the existing residual-capable block implementation. This must preserve explicit configuration/forced-inlining policy, type eligibility and cost/stage behavior; it is not a solution for disabled or unsupported block execution.

A KQP-owned row residual join lowering could evaluate each original pair directly, but would require new buffering/spilling/resource and evaluation-count tests. Reusing the current cross-join materialization blindly would increase OOM risk and is not a small verified fix.

candidate_extensions.classification: Existing Pickle admission rejects nonpersistable values. Preserve occurrences through a compatible join implementation or explicit once-only identity; do not claim serialized support.

source_evidence.contract: Float/Double packing canonicalizes bits only in the Stable template; ordinary Pickle preserves the raw representation.
Stable canonicalization merges signed-zero encodings and NaN payloads.
Timezone packing stores the timezone identifier as well as the temporal value.
Optional presence is encoded separately and nested optionals recurse.
List packing traverses list contents; this is not merely a constant-time identity read.
Struct/tuple fields are packed in their type-defined order.
Nonstable dictionaries follow iterator order; stable dictionaries may sort entries.
Pickle requires persistability and returns nonoptional String; Unpickle accepts an explicit persistable target type and returns exactly that type.
CanDuplicateAggregation deliberately ignores input type and reduction order; it is not a byte-stability guarantee for serialized floating identity.
Without retained sharing, secondary consumers receive independently evaluated admitted producer copies.
The flow counter belongs to a computation evaluation; stream and list iterators have separate counters. There is no cross-task uniqueness or shared-producer planner contract.
Existing block join lowering builds residual filter lambdas; ordinary row fallback does not offer the same general residual interface.
Existing row cross join materializes the right relation. Extending it to outer residual joins requires explicit resource behavior rather than assuming scalability.

acceptance_policy: These outstanding cases remain part of archived C31 scope. They are neither counted as fixed nor relabeled away. A future restricted extension can add proven cases, but remaining families retain explicit outstanding acceptance.
